newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia completes overhaul of major bank.
newsitem.headline: Croatia completes overhaul of major bank.

text.p: The Croatian government has succesfully completed the overhaul of one of its major banks, the ailing Rijecka Banka, burdened by insolvency of its shipbuilding creditors.

The state radio quoted Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa on Monday as praising Rijecka's rehabilitation, which he said had helped cut prices of capital. He said the overhaul created conditions for Rijecka to become a participant in European and world markets.
"Interest rates in Croatia fell dramatically, partly also thanks to the rehabilitaion of Rijecka Banka," Matesa told the radio.
The rates fell mainly due to weaker demand from Rijecka and another ailing bank, Splitska Banka. Both banks got cash injections in the government's drive to recapitalise them.
Rijecka used to be among top five banks in Croatia. The overhaul, which began this spring, will enable it to continue supporting the country's seaside tourism and shipbuilding.
The government hopes the banking overhaul will revitalise the economy and include foreign capital in development programmes, Matesa said.
Croatia's economy has been in trouble since the 1991 war that followed the country's secession from communist Yugoslavia.

National Bank Governor Marko Skreb announced on Monday an influx of Austrian, German, Korean and Italian capital into Croatia in 1997. That would create more competition and further reduce interest rates, he said. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
